neighboring_unit_entries.title: From isolated irrationality results to dimension growth for odd zeta values
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: The introduction reframes the target from proving individual irrationalities to producing lower bounds for the dimension of the span of 1 and odd zeta values, making explicit the collective linear-independence objective that governs the construction.

neighboring_unit_entries.title: Symmetric rational functions produce linear forms supported only on odd zeta values
neighboring_unit_entries.why_material: A parameterized rational function is differentiated and summed at integers; partial fractions plus its reflection parity cancel unwanted terms and express the result as a rational linear form in a controlled band of odd zeta values. This is the central representation change from a hypergeometric-type sum to arithmetic information.

related_synthesis_entries.claim: The theorem families arise by choosing parameters so the odd-zeta support lands on a desired interval while the combined exponential budget stays favorable, converting a collective linear form into at-least-one-irrational conclusions rather than identifying a particular irrational value.
related_synthesis_entries.limit: Exact panel endpoints and numerical parameter checks require verification from the typeset article.

spontaneous.spontaneous_reading: The unit turns one construction into a portfolio of outputs and, more importantly, exposes the proof as a four-part budget: saddle-point smallness, improved denominators, coefficient growth, and a final linear-independence conversion. The theorem panels are parameter-dependent projections of that common mechanism.

directed.source_grounded_mathematics: The source states finite collections of odd zeta values containing at least one irrational number, linear-independence assertions involving 1 and selected odd zeta values, and a lower bound for δ(a). It explicitly attributes the proofs to saddle-point analysis, improved denominator estimates, coefficient asymptotics, and final deductions in Section 6.
directed.conceptual_reading: The roadmap decomposes the argument into independent obligations: make a rational linear form small, make its denominators sufficiently economical, control the size of its coefficients, and apply a criterion translating those rates into irrationality or dimension.
directed.representation_or_bridge: Parameter choices connect the support interval of a common linear-form construction to different finite zeta panels, while the rate estimates connect that construction to a linear-independence criterion.
directed.boundary_or_failure: These are statements and a dependency map, not demonstrations. At-least-one-irrational conclusions remain collective and do not determine which member of a panel is irrational.
directed.uncertainty: The qualitative theorem portfolio and section map are readable, but exact endpoints, constants, and inequalities in the extracted displays require PDF verification.

supported: The span states three kinds of outputs: finite-panel at-least-one irrationality, existence of selected linearly independent zeta values with 1, and a lower bound for δ(a).

The author's roadmap explicitly names saddle-point calculations, denominator improvement, coefficient asymptotics, and final deductions, so the candidate's budget decomposition is a useful reading of the section map.
